spec_match.rationale: Uses the real product-shaped composition the feature exists for: AbortSignal.any([user, AbortSignal.timeout()]) on a streamed fetch, branching the catch handler on the forwarded reason.

interactive.rationale: Real download with live progress derived from the route's newline framing (robust to network chunk coalescing/splitting — Codex review round 1), a working cancel button, and a selectable deadline; three genuinely different outcomes are reachable (complete, user cancel, timeout).

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index blurb promises diagnosable cancellation causes; the page shows exactly that, including the honest ambiguity message where the browser drops the cause.

edge_cases.rationale: Missing AbortSignal.any/timeout is feature-detected with an explicit capability message; a Response.body that is not exposed as a ReadableStream now gets its own labelled capability-gap message (Copilot review round 1) instead of the generic error branch; the pre-153 generic AbortError branch refuses to guess the cause; real network failure is separated from aborts.

references.rationale: Links the ChromeStatus entry and MDN for AbortSignal.timeout()/any().

conformance.rationale: The suite's timeout-reason-timeouterror assertion pins the TimeoutError vocabulary this page branches on; the post-response assertions pin the forwarding it needs.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 via CDP: all three outcomes driven — timeout at 1200ms (honest ambiguity message), user cancel at ~900ms (progress 40%, same honest message on this build), and full completion (progress 100%, byte count). Console/network clean.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts record diagnosed cause (user/timeout/ambiguous/error) and the completion path with byte counts.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables only; progress uses accent-color on the design system's black; select/button pairs inherit the shared control styling.

accessibility.rationale: Labelled select, native buttons with 44px targets, progress carries an aria-label, and both the log and the product-facing user message are role=status aria-live=polite regions (the user message gained live semantics in Codex round 2).

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP matrix: overflow 0 on both classes, controls wrap into rows on 360px without clipping. Harness responsive-check confirms ok on both classes after the same-origin failure-scoping fix (Codex review round 1).

openQuestions.title: Demonstrate the precise user-cancel and timeout diagnoses on Chrome 153+
openQuestions.detail: On this pre-153 build both stop paths honestly collapse into the ambiguity message. On Chrome 153+ the UserCancelledError and TimeoutError branches should each render their precise product message — verify both and update the critique.

guidanceConsulted.query: cancel in-flight fetch abort signal timeout streaming download progress
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Combine user-driven and deadline-driven cancellation with AbortSignal.any and keep the UI truthful about which fired.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: AbortSignal.any([user, timeout]) composition, disabled-state management during the download, and an explicit refusal to guess the cause when the browser drops it.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: npx modern-web-guidance@latest search run 2026-08-09; full-session-analytics and deprioritize-background-fetches were the closest AbortController/fetch guides.

summary: Verified with headless Chromium 141 via CDP: completion (100%, 249 bytes), user cancel (progress 40%), and 1200ms timeout all driven; the pre-153 ambiguity is stated honestly instead of guessed; console/network clean; both viewport classes inspected. Re-verified after the review-round guards: same clean behavior on this stream-capable engine.
